title: Pakistan Movement
lines: The Pakistan Movement is the biggest Pakistan Studies topic in USAT. Questions ask for the year of an event, the leader linked to a resolution or session, the aim of a reform, or the place where something happened. The span is 1857 to 1947. Learn the timeline in order; cause and effect then make the dates easy to remember.
## After 1857: Muslim revival
- The War of Independence (1857) failed; the last Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah Zafar, was exiled to Rangoon, and the British Crown took over from the East India Company (1858).

- Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind on the causes of the revolt and urged Muslims to take up modern education. He founded the Scientific Society (1864) and the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental School at Aligarh (1875), which became a college in 1877. This was the Aligarh Movement.
- The Hindi-Urdu controversy (1867, Banaras) convinced Sir Syed that Hindus and Muslims were separate nations, an early form of the Two-Nation Theory.
- The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885. Sir Syed advised Muslims to stay away from it.
## Timeline 1905–1947
| Year | Event
| 1905 | Partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon; Muslims of East Bengal welcomed it
| 1906 | Simla Deputation under Sir Aga Khan III meets Lord Minto (1 October); All-India Muslim League founded at Dhaka (30 December)
| 1909 | Minto-Morley Reforms grant separate electorates
| 1911 | Partition of Bengal annulled
| 1913 | Jinnah joins the Muslim League
| 1916 | Lucknow Pact: Congress accepts separate electorates; Jinnah called Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity
| 1919 | Rowlatt Act; Jallianwala Bagh at Amritsar; Government of India Act introduces dyarchy
| 1919–1924 | Khilafat Movement led by Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Shaukat Ali
| 1927–1928 | Simon Commission (no Indian member); Nehru Report (1928) rejects separate electorates
| 1929 | Jinnah's Fourteen Points
| 1930 | Allama Iqbal's Allahabad Address calls for a Muslim state in north-west India
| 1930–1932 | Round Table Conferences in London
| 1933 | Chaudhry Rahmat Ali's pamphlet Now or Never proposes the name Pakistan
| 1935 | Government of India Act: provincial autonomy
| 1937 | Provincial elections; Congress ministries formed
| 1939 | Day of Deliverance (22 December) after Congress ministries resign
| 1940 | Lahore Resolution, moved on 23 March by A. K. Fazlul Huq at Minto Park, Lahore
| 1942 | Cripps Mission; Quit India Movement
| 1944 | Gandhi-Jinnah talks in Bombay
| 1945 | Simla Conference fails
| 1945–1946 | General elections: the League wins all Muslim seats in the Central Assembly
| 1946 | Cabinet Mission Plan; Direct Action Day (16 August)
| 1947 | 3 June Plan by Lord Mountbatten; Indian Independence Act (July); Pakistan comes into being on 14 August
## The Lahore Resolution

The Muslim League session at Lahore (22–24 March 1940) was presided over by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah. The resolution, moved by Fazlul Huq on 23 March, demanded that the Muslim-majority areas in the north-west and east of India be grouped into independent states. The Hindu press called it the Pakistan Resolution, and the name stuck. Minar-e-Pakistan now stands at the site, in today's Iqbal Park.
## Key leaders
| Leader | Remember
| Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah | born Karachi, 25 December 1876; first Governor-General; died 11 September 1948
| Allama Muhammad Iqbal | born Sialkot, 1877; poet-philosopher; Allahabad Address 1930; died 1938
| Liaquat Ali Khan | first Prime Minister; moved the Objectives Resolution; assassinated in Rawalpindi, 1951
| Fatima Jinnah | Madar-e-Millat, the Mother of the Nation
| Sir Aga Khan III | led the Simla Deputation; first permanent president of the League
| Chaudhry Rahmat Ali | coined the name Pakistan (1933)
> Which reform first gave Muslims separate electorates?  (A) Lucknow Pact  (B) Minto-Morley Reforms  (C) Government of India Act 1935  (D) Nehru Report
> B. Separate electorates came with the 1909 reforms. Congress accepted them in the 1916 Lucknow Pact; the Nehru Report tried to remove them.
> Muslims celebrated the Day of Deliverance in 1939 because  (A) Pakistan was created  (B) the Congress ministries resigned  (C) the Simon Commission left  (D) Bengal was partitioned
> B. The League saw the end of the 1937–39 Congress ministries as relief from unfair rule.
## Traps
! The Lahore Resolution was moved by Fazlul Huq, but the session was presided over by Jinnah.
! The name Pakistan came from Rahmat Ali (1933), not from Iqbal's 1930 address, which did not use the word.
! The Muslim League was founded in Dhaka, not Lahore or Aligarh.
## Quick check
- 1857 revolt; 1875 Aligarh; 1885 Congress; 1906 League; 1909 separate electorates.
- 1916 Lucknow; 1928 Nehru Report; 1929 Fourteen Points; 1930 Allahabad; 1933 the name.
- 1940 Lahore Resolution; 1946 Cabinet Mission; 3 June 1947 Plan; 14 August 1947.
